title: How a rocket gets off the pad in one go
dek: Four parts take turns in every launch. Follow one countdown through all of them, and see what each one waits for before it hands over.
question: A launch has one chance. How does every part know it is safe to go?
opening: A launch has one chance, and any part can stop it. So how does each part know that it is safe to go?

stops.say: The launch pad decides when the rocket can leave.

beats.label: Countdown runs
beats.say: First, the countdown runs to zero.

beats.label: Gyro not settled
beats.say: If the gyro still moves, the clamps hold the rocket down.

beats.label: Clamps open
beats.say: Once guidance is steady, they open.

beats.label: Spark
beats.say: It makes a spark, and if the spark misses, it tries again.

beats.label: Pushes the rocket
beats.say: So the thrust pushes the rocket up.

stops.say: Guidance keeps the rocket pointed the right way. The pad waits for its gyro to settle.
As the rocket climbs, guidance steers the push where it must go.
Before any of this, CI tests every change.

beats.label: Engine tests
beats.say: First, it runs the engine tests.

beats.label: Countdown tests
beats.say: Then it runs the countdown tests.

beats.label: Every test
beats.say: Once every test passes, the change can fly.

closing: Each part waits for the part before it. That is how the rocket goes in one try.
